## QA-61-01 — MEDIUM — The register omits the later same-profile-tab recording decision

**Class:** confirmed documentation/decision-register defect. **Evidence status:** confirmed text mismatch; no runtime defect asserted. **Affected:** AC-01, AC-02; Flow 09 F09-AC-30, `OPEN-09-13-LEASE`; recording-access technical slice.

**Reproduce:** read `_docs/frontend-implementation-contract.md` lines 68–89 (current decisions and selected slices), 104 (Flow 09 gate inventory), 121 (resume proof), and 129–138 (resolved/superseded wording). Then compare `_docs/frontend-flows/00-shared-contract.md` lines 406–409 and the 2026-10-25 owner receipt lines 15, 27, 29.

**Expected:** the shared technical register records that only one browser tab per project may capture/accept, including tabs sharing the durable client/session, while distinguishing that settled product choice from remaining production lease/disconnect/fencing evidence. It should name the affected #77 owner/AC and the current mock/real evidence boundary.

**Actual:** the register's recording slice discusses account/client/session grants and 45-second mock leases, and its Flow 09 row names remaining lease mechanics, but never records the new tab-level exclusivity rule. Its owner-decision section still frames its decisions as supplied on 2026-10-23. The policy-sync receipt explicitly says the register update covered only Flow 06's source-policy summary. The automated audit finds the same-profile-tab concept in shared/Flow 09 and not in this register. Thus a consumer relying on the issue's promised decision index can miss the important distinction between session identity and recording-tab ownership.

**Impact:** future facade/real-adapter work can treat a shared signed-in session as sufficient ownership, or waste a new owner question on a settled policy. This is meaningful contract drift at an ownership seam. The later shared/Flow 09 authority still wins; this review does not allege that current application tabs can capture concurrently.

**Scoped recommendation:** add a dated settled-decision row and update only the recording technical slice/resume mapping to link F09-AC-30 and the recorded owner answer. Preserve the distinction between per-tab ownership and durable auth identity, and leave production timing/disconnect/fencing unapproved. Link current evidence rather than copying old pass text. **Next validation:** independent text read-back of register/shared/Flow 09 alignment; a separately scoped two-tab runtime check if an implementation change is made.

**Screenshot applicability:** no screenshot can establish ownership fencing. The representative New dub images show the shared shell only; the proof for this finding is the source mismatch and [document-audit.json](evidence/document-audit.json), not an image. An unrelated recording screenshot would add no valid proof.

## QA-61-02 — MEDIUM — The compact desktop decision lacks a job-specific density exception

**Class:** requirement/design flaw in the adopted cross-cutting contract, visible through its consumers. **Evidence status:** measured facts confirmed; usability interpretation is a review judgment. **Affected:** AC-02's rationale/source-inventory slice; adoption explicit exception 1; token desktop-density role. This is not a new review of #81 or #78 acceptance.

**Reproduce:** complete visible mock registration, land on New dub at 1440×900, inspect its sole file-selection action. Switch RU and inspect at 1440×700. Resize the same state from 767px to 768px. Compare captures 02–06 and metrics after fonts settle.

**Expected quality:** the source's compact menu/toolbar vocabulary can remain, but the principal action in a sparse task-entry screen should have a readable, easily acquired role that reflects its importance. Density should be chosen for the job and input context, with compact behavior justified where it buys useful information density.

**Actual measured facts:**

| State | Visible file-action geometry | Label role | Viewport/document width |
|---|---|---|---|
| EN wide, 1440×900 | 960×28px | Mabry Pro 13px/20px | 1440/1440 |
| RU short, 1440×700 | 960×28px | Mabry Pro 13px/20px | 1440/1440 |
| RU phone, 390×844 | 358×48px | Mabry Pro 16px/24px | 390/390 |
| RU at 767×900 | 735×48px | Mabry Pro 16px/24px | 767/767 |
| RU at 768×900 | 704×28px | Mabry Pro 13px/20px | 768/768 |

At 1440 the one main action is a very wide, thin neutral strip with small centered text. Large unused space means compact height buys no denser useful content here. Increasing width by one pixel at the breakpoint reduces its height by 20px and text by 3px, even though the user job has not changed. The long hit width helps pointer acquisition; the concern is vertical tolerance, readability and hierarchy, not a claim that the whole control is tiny in both dimensions.

The adopted contract deliberately selects this density: tokens lines 88–90 and 164; adoption lines 57–59; workflow compact-button paragraph. `frontend/src/App.css` lines 337–356 implements the source sizes. The result follows the chosen source rather than proving an accidental CSS mismatch. A size meeting a numeric minimum can still be a poor task-entry default. This review does **not** label 28px an automatic WCAG violation, and no user study or target-error rate was measured.

**Impact:** the most important next action looks subordinate to 16px body copy and a secondary Manage projects link. Users with lower visual acuity or imperfect pointer control receive a weaker affordance, while wide touch devices inherit the desktop rule solely from viewport width.

**Scoped recommendation:** refine the shared density contract to distinguish compact navigation/menu actions from primary task actions. Consider a 40–48px task-action role with 16px/24px Mabry while retaining the selected source shape, neutral palette, state treatment and compact chrome. This is a proposed contract change requiring deliberate owner/design review, not authorization for a silent fix. **Next validation:** compare the same EN/RU task-entry screens at wide/short/767/768, 200% zoom and coarse-pointer input, checking actual click targets, hierarchy and flow completion. Avoid scaling every desktop control indiscriminately.

## What works and supporting states

The register's central separation of contract acceptance, mock evidence, and production readiness is sound. It names source selection/billing binding, independent revisions, stable operation identity, zero-turn preservation, explicit-exit priority and displayed-generation download identity. Its current short-source rejection is correctly described as an upload-eligibility rule, without converting it into a minimum take duration. The later #76 deferment remains a separate real-adapter boundary; no mock pass is used here to close it.

In the fresh visible states, Mabry font faces loaded, phone copy and primary controls remain readable, six measured document widths match their viewports, and the shell changes cleanly at the selected breakpoint. Mock OTP and Google notices explicitly avoid suggesting real delivery/contact. The neutral sign-in error retains user-entered values and an obvious focus outline. Phone sign-in is vertically scrollable; the bottom content below the screenshot edge is not called clipping.

![OTP notice clearly limits email claim to a local mock](evidence/01-register-otp-en-desktop.png)

![Neutral credential error, retained input and visible focus](evidence/07-signin-error-focus-en-desktop.png)

![RU phone error and mock-provider notice](evidence/08-signin-error-ru-phone.png)

## Coverage gaps and next proof

This is a bounded decision-contract review, not full product acceptance. No recording capture, tab-contention runtime, microphone hardware, browser codec matrix, source upload, millisecond quote authorization, zero-turn replacement, credit mutation, result generation/download, production persistence, security/privacy enforcement, OAuth, email, payment or deletion backend was exercised. AC-03 runtime consequences remain unverified here. The original issue's document-only acceptance remains separate from these omissions.

200% browser zoom, forced colors, screen-reader behavior, reduced-motion timing, dialogs, in-flight cancellation, loading transitions, long project names, and every EN/RU permutation were not run. EN phone and RU full-height desktop were not separately captured; representative EN desktop, RU short desktop/phone, and RU breakpoint states were prioritized. No full suite or design-skill global inspector was run; custom bounded browser metrics and visual inspection were used, preserving the owner-selected Affect UI rules over generic skill styling defaults.

No screenshot proves security, backend durability, idempotency, session expiry policy, tab fencing, financial correctness, or actual media generation. Follow-ups above are recommendations only; no issue state or acceptance was changed.
